name: mkldnn_linear_backward_weights
description: Representative ATen overload (not an exclusive ABI): aten::mkldnn_linear_backward_weights(Tensor grad_output, Tensor input, Tensor weight, bool bias_defined) -> (Tensor, Tensor). This representative signature is selected only as the contract anchor; it is NOT exclusive, and the original Gems pytest owns the full contract of overloads, keyword arguments, returns, errors, aliasing and mutation and must not be narrowed to this one signature. All supplied registered schemas, verbatim: aten::mkldnn_linear_backward_weights(Tensor grad_output, Tensor input, Tensor weight, bool bias_defined) -> (Tensor, Tensor) ; aten::mkldnn_linear_backward_weights.out(Tensor grad_output, Tensor input, Tensor weight, bool bias_defined, *, Tensor(a!) out0, Tensor(b!) out1) -> (Tensor(a!), Tensor(b!)). Semantics derived from the correctness tests: MkldnnCPU is the only registered dispatch key, so grad_output and input must be mkldnn-layout CPU tensors while weight is a dense float32 CPU tensor; bias_defined (bool) controls whether grad_bias is computed. The default (out-of-place) overload returns two freshly allocated dense CPU float32 tensors: grad_weight shaped (out_features, in_features) and grad_bias shaped (out_features,), which is an undefined 0-dim placeholder when bias_defined is False. Probed operand dtypes are float32, float16 and bfloat16 (mkldnn operands), and results are always float32; int8/uint8 mkldnn operands and dense/non-float32 weights are rejected by the native operator. Overload-dependent behavior kept in pytest and not expressed here: the out overload takes required keyword-only out0/out1 buffers, mutates them (the schema marks them Tensor(a!)/Tensor(b!)) and returns those same caller buffers, so its results alias its own out arguments; the representative default overload mutates no parameters and returns no aliases. Error behavior — dense operands without a CPU kernel, non-mkldnn grad_output/input, non-float32 weight, unsupported mkldnn operand dtypes, rank-1 operands, batch mismatch and empty contraction dimension K — is also asserted by the original pytest and is not part of this representative signature.
